an10.23:1.1: “Bhikkhus, there are things to be abandoned by body, not by speech.
an10.23:1.2: There are things to be abandoned by speech, not by body.
an10.23:1.3: There are things to be abandoned neither by body nor by speech but by having repeatedly seen with wisdom.
an10.23:2.1: “And what, bhikkhus, are the things to be abandoned by body, not by speech?
an10.23:2.2: Here, a bhikkhu has committed a particular unwholesome deed with the body.
an10.23:2.3: His wise fellow monks investigate him and say thus:
an10.23:2.4: ‘You have committed a particular unwholesome deed with the body.
an10.23:2.5: It would really be good if you would abandon bodily misconduct and develop bodily good conduct.’
an10.23:2.6: When his wise fellow monks investigate him and speak to him, he abandons bodily misconduct and develops bodily good conduct.
an10.23:2.7: These are called things to be abandoned by body, not by speech.
an10.23:3.1: “And what are the things to be abandoned by speech, not by body?
an10.23:3.2: Here, a bhikkhu has committed a particular unwholesome deed by speech.
an10.23:3.3: His wise fellow monks investigate him and say thus:
an10.23:3.4: ‘You have committed a particular unwholesome deed by speech.
an10.23:3.5: It would really be good if you would abandon verbal misconduct and develop verbal good conduct.’
an10.23:3.6: When his wise fellow monks investigate him and speak to him, he abandons verbal misconduct and develops verbal good conduct.
an10.23:3.7: These are called things to be abandoned by speech, not by body.
an10.23:4.1: “And what are the things to be abandoned neither by body nor by speech but by having repeatedly seen with wisdom?
an10.23:4.2: Greed is to be abandoned neither by body nor by speech but by having repeatedly seen with wisdom.
an10.23:4.9: Miserliness is to be abandoned neither by body nor by speech but by having repeatedly seen with wisdom.
an10.23:5.1: “Evil envy, bhikkhus, is to be abandoned neither by body nor by speech but by having repeatedly seen with wisdom.
an10.23:5.3: Here, a householder or householder’s son is prospering in wealth or grain, in silver or gold.
an10.23:5.4: A slave or dependent might think of him:
an10.23:5.5: ‘Oh, may this householder or householder’s son not prosper in wealth or grain, in silver or gold!’
an10.23:5.6: Or else an ascetic or brahmin gains robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicines and provisions for the sick.
an10.23:5.7: Another ascetic or brahmin might think of him:
an10.23:5.8: ‘Oh, may this venerable one not gain robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicines and provisions for the sick!’
an10.23:5.9: This is called evil envy. Evil envy is to be abandoned neither by body nor by speech but by having repeatedly seen with wisdom.
an10.23:6.1: “Evil desire, bhikkhus, is to be abandoned neither by body nor by speech but by having repeatedly seen with wisdom.
an10.23:6.3: Here, one without faith desires: ‘Let them know me as one endowed with faith.’
an10.23:6.4: An immoral person desires: ‘Let them know me as virtuous.’
an10.23:6.5: One with little learning desires: ‘Let them know me as learned.’
an10.23:6.6: One who delights in company desires: ‘Let them know me as solitary.’
an10.23:6.7: One who is lazy desires: ‘Let them know me as energetic.’
an10.23:6.8: One who is muddle-minded desires: ‘Let them know me as mindful.’
an10.23:6.9: One who is unconcentrated desires: ‘Let them know me as concentrated.’
an10.23:6.10: One who is unwise desires: ‘Let them know me as wise.’
an10.23:6.11: One whose taints are not destroyed desires: ‘Let them know me as one whose taints are destroyed.’
an10.23:6.13: Evil desire is to be abandoned neither by body nor by speech but by having repeatedly seen with wisdom.
an10.23:7.1: “If, bhikkhus, greed overcomes that bhikkhu and continues on;
an10.23:7.10: evil desire overcomes that bhikkhu and continues on,
an10.23:7.12: ‘This venerable one does not understand in such a way that he would have no greed; thus greed overcomes him and continues on.
an10.23:7.13: This venerable one does not understand in such a way that he would have no hatred …
an10.23:7.21: no evil desire; thus evil desire overcomes him and continues on.’
an10.23:8.1: “If, bhikkhus, greed does not overcome that bhikkhu and continue on;
an10.23:8.10: evil desire does not overcome that bhikkhu and continue on,
an10.23:8.12: ‘This venerable one understands in such a way that he would have no greed; thus greed does not overcome him and continue on.
an10.23:8.13: This venerable one understands in such a way that he would have no hatred …
an10.23:8.21: no evil desire; thus evil desire does not overcome him and continue on.’”
